summary: 36-year-old man with 4 months of heartburn and acid regurgitation, worse lying down, relieved by antacids; no alarm features. NICE CG184: lifestyle advice and full-dose PPI for 4 (–8) weeks; no endoscopy.

inputs.hpi: Four months of burning behind the breastbone after meals and acid coming up into the throat, worse lying flat and after late meals and beer. Antacids help. No difficulty swallowing, no weight loss, no vomiting, no black stools.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Typical GORD without alarm features, age 36 — empirical full-dose PPI for 4 weeks and lifestyle measures.

emergencyLevel.note: The HPI lists alarm features as absent ("no difficulty swallowing, no weight loss…"); negated features must not escalate.
emergencyLevel.proposedFix: adaptive-triage: strip negated clauses ("no/denies/without X") before RED_FLAGS, GI_BLEED_TERMS and vomiting rules.

mustNotAlarm.note: Any alarm that fires here comes from reading a negated feature as present.

guideline.name: NICE CG184 — Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease and dyspepsia in adults: investigation and management
guideline.section: GORD without alarm features: lifestyle advice; full-dose PPI for 4 (or 8) weeks; refer for endoscopy only per NG12 or if symptoms persist
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Clinical guideline CG184. London: NICE; 2014 (last updated 2019).

guideline.name: NICE NG12 — Suspected cancer: recognition and referral (oesophageal and stomach cancer)
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. NICE guideline NG12. London: NICE; 2015 (last updated 2023).

rationale: Base GORD case with alarm features explicitly absent in the HPI. Tests over-triage caused by negation ("no weight loss" read as weight loss). The web CC template name contains "GORD" (the only heartburn template), so the differential expectation is partly circular and kept quality.
